rationale: This is a data-availability splice of two signals already in the archive (TotalCashUsesRequirement and EarningsBasedCashUses) with no new economic claim — the only difference is a missing-value convention, so any gain is a coverage patch rather than a testable mechanism.

The MIN operator's only incremental content relative to the strongest cash-based archive signal is a penalty of max(0, oancf − ib), i.e. it downgrades *low-accrual* firms, which runs against the direction of the well-published accruals anomaly, and because MIN requires both inputs the construct also forfeits the breadth the reasoning claims to exploit.

Adding acquisition outlays to the uses side is a modest but economically coherent respecification that the archive's goodwill results genuinely motivate, though it sits close to the published net-external-financing/total-investment anomaly and collapses to the existing leader for most non-acquirers, limiting the potential increment.

The two legs are conceptually distinct (size of the required raise versus convertibility of internal resources) and share no inputs, so this is a legitimate test of whether the inventory-illiquidity effect operates through the funding constraint rather than a repackaging of the oancf/lt coverage leg.

A three-year moving average of the archive's leading requirement signal is a mechanical smoothing variant, and since the level was already shown to dominate the innovation, the incremental information content of averaging a slow-moving state is minimal.

The conditioning leg RANK(NEG(oancf/lt)) has already been paired with five different partners in the archive with uniformly similar negative alphas, so this mostly re-tests that leg; moreover the stated justification is internally wrong — aqc is zero for most firms, so the composition ratio has exactly the tied-zero mass the reasoning claims to avoid, and it is unstable when capx+aqc is near zero or aqc is negative.
